Hero Billboard Chart JP.text: The Hero Billboard Chart JP is the official ranking of Japan's professional heroes, published by the Hero Public Safety Commission twice a year. It weighs three things: incidents resolved, social contribution and public approval. Combat strength is not a category, so a quiet rescue specialist can outrank a famous brawler, and a popular hero with few cases can slide. The full chart runs far down the list of active heroes, but public attention goes to the top ten, announced at a televised event with speeches, interviews and heavy press coverage. A ranking moves an agency's fortunes: a rise brings sponsors, sidekick applicants, fan mail and bigger cases, and a fall can cost all of them. At the start of this academic year the order at the top is long familiar. All Might is Number One and has held the top spot for so long that most young people cannot remember anyone else there; his lead over the field is enormous. Endeavor is Number Two, with the most incidents resolved in history and approval numbers far below his results. Hawks is Number Three, the youngest hero ever to reach the top ten. Fans argue about the rest constantly, on talk shows, in school hallways and on online forums, and predicting the next chart is a national pastime. Pros publicly claim not to care about their numbers, and most of them check anyway.
